site.title: mmlabs
site.intro: mmlabs is where Ming designs, builds and runs his own web apps. Each one takes a real, everyday problem at work and solves it end to end, from product idea and architecture to a running service.
about: mmlabs is the personal software lab of Ming, a solution architect and technical manager. It is a place to try ideas properly: write the brief, design the system, ship it, and keep the ones that earn their place.
The apps are independent web applications, each with its own codebase and data. They are being brought together under one shared sign-in, so a single account will work across all of them.

apps.name: Ricotdin
apps.summary: Records online meetings from the browser, with no bot in the call, then turns them into a transcript, summary, to-dos and a chat that answers with timestamps.
problem: Decisions happen in meetings, and the details leave with them. Taking notes means only half following the conversation.
Recording tools usually ask for something in return: a bot that joins the call and announces itself, a desktop app to install, or output that only works well in English.
steps: Capture the meeting tab and your microphone from the browser, mixed into one audio-only stream.
Get a speaker-labelled transcript with timestamps: who said what, and when.
A summary, structured notes, action items and calendar mentions are extracted automatically.
Chat across one meeting or all of them. Every answer points back to the moment it was said.
features: No bot, no install
Works in the browser alongside Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and Zoom. Nothing joins the call.
Speaker-labelled transcript
Clickable timestamps jump the audio player to the exact moment.
Summary and notes
A short summary plus structured notes on topics, decisions and next steps.
To-dos and calendar
Action items with owners and dates, exportable as .ics. Times are never made up.
Grounded chat
Answers only from what was said, cites the timestamp, and says “not found” instead of guessing.
Multilingual
Transcript, notes and answers come back in the language of the meeting.
apps.audience: Consultants, project leads, founders and client-facing teams who run back-to-back calls and need a reliable record afterwards, in their own language.
tech: Unified web app (UI and backend in one codebase)
Private object storage with signed URLs
Language model for summaries, extraction and Q&A
apps.privacy: Audio is stored privately and reached only through short-lived signed URLs. The AI tier used does not train on user data, and each user can only see their own meetings.
roadmap: Recording, processing pipeline, transcript, grounded chat, to-dos and calendar, meeting library, and role-based sign-in.
A durable job queue, monitoring, security hardening and a clear data retention policy.
Real speaker names, library-wide search, summary emails, calendar sync and folders.

apps.name: SeatMGT
apps.tagline: Every seat, every device, on one map.
apps.summary: Turns the who-sits-where spreadsheet into a living floor plan: seats mapped to network ports, devices tracked to owners, moves handled by request and approval.
problem: Seats are wired to specific network ports, and devices change hands. People take a second desk, lend a monitor or move across the room, and the tracking sheet is out of date the moment they do.
The result is not knowing which port a machine is on, who owns what, or where free capacity actually is. Every reshuffle becomes a manual hunt.
steps: A user picks an open seat on the map and submits a request.
A manager approves it, or assigns someone directly.
The person's machine becomes the seat's primary device, tied to that seat's network port.
When they leave, the seat opens and the device is released. No orphaned records.
features: Visual layout designer
Drag seats onto a grid that mirrors the real room. Each tile is a real seat record.
Seats mapped to ports
Every seat gets a code like C302-01 tied to its network port. Status comes from who is sitting there.
Request and approve
Users request, managers approve or assign, with a clear trail of who decided what.
Device ownership
One primary device per seat, owned by whoever sits there. Spare devices wait in inventory.
Members and groups
Each person's seats and devices in one view, with group and project labels for context.
Access and audit
Roles enforced on both the API and the interface, with an audit log of every move.
apps.audience: Facilities and IT leads who own the floor, team managers who keep seating moving, and everyone who needs a desk and a working machine.
roadmap: Project setup with sign-in, layout designer, and seat and device management.
Containerised deployment, a real database behind the data layer, then feedback and iteration.

apps.name: CaleChip
apps.tagline: See who's out before it's too late.
apps.summary: A shared calendar where everyone declares planned leave and work-from-home days early, with a warning when too much of the team is away on the same day.
problem: Leave plans live in chat threads and in people's heads. By the time a formal request reaches HR, it is too late for anyone to adjust.
Around public holidays everyone targets the same bridge days without knowing it, trips booked months ahead surface at the last minute, and a lead has no quick way to see how next month looks.
features: Plan leave and WFH
Full or half days, several days selected in one drag.
Tentative plans
Mark a plan as not final yet. It is still visible to the team and still counts.
Overload warning
A warning while you pick dates if more than half the team would be away. It warns, it never blocks.
Approval with a gold star
An admin approves entries, so everyone knows which plans are settled.
Vietnamese holidays and bridge days
Public holidays are built in, and the app flags bridge days and how many people have already taken them.
Week, month and year views
Week for coordinating work, month for everyday use, year for spotting overlaps far in advance.
apps.audience: Teams that want to coordinate time off early, and leads who need the big picture at a glance.
scopeOut: Leave balances and quotas, which stay with HR
The official leave request process, which it sits in front of
roadmap: Sign-in, teams, leave and WFH entries, month view, overload warning, Vietnamese holidays.
Week and year views, approval flow, tentative tag, bridge-day detection.
Reminders, a weekly digest to the team channel, export for HR, recurring entries.

apps.name: Engineering Risk Intelligence
apps.tagline: See delivery risk before it becomes a surprise.
apps.summary: Turns Jira, pull request and CI signals into a prioritized, explainable action list for the people monitoring delivery, with rule-based, auditable risk decisions.

apps.name: ContractPilot
apps.tagline: Catch breaking API changes before staging.
apps.summary: Plugs into a service repository, reads how services call each other, and generates contract tests for both consumer and provider, keeping only the tests that pass when run.

apps.name: CertTracker
apps.summary: Replaces the team's certificate spreadsheet with one shared record: everyone keeps their own certificates current with proof, managers see their teams at a glance, and expiry reminders arrive in time.

platform.title: One sign-in, coming soon
platform.text: Authen is the shared sign-in service for mmlabs. Once it is in place, you log in once and move between every app without signing in again. New apps plug into the same sign-in, so the lab can keep growing without new passwords.
